close_reason: Single-sourced via new pub const MAILBOX_FILTER_CONDITION_KEYS at jmap-mail-types/src/mailbox.rs:262 (co-located with MailboxFilterCondition). Drift-check unit test mailbox_filter_condition_keys_matches_struct_fields serialises a fully-populated struct literal and compares keys against the const, so adding a field without updating the const fails cargo test -p jmap-mail-types. The struct literal in the test uses non-exhaustive field listing, so adding a field without setting it ALSO fails to compile. mail-server/src/mailbox.rs:220 now references jmap_mail_types::MAILBOX_FILTER_CONDITION_KEYS instead of the private const. Behaviour preserved: unknown filter keys still produce unsupportedFilter per RFC 8620 §5.5.
description:
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs:228 maintains 'const KNOWN_FILTER_KEYS: &[&str] = &["parentId", "name", "role", "hasAnyRole", "isSubscribed"];' which is hand-synchronised with the fields of MailboxFilterCondition in jmap-mail-types. The maintenance comment at lines 223-227 acknowledges the drift risk explicitly: 'If a new field is added to MailboxFilterCondition, add its wire name here. Drift causes filter conditions to be rejected with unsupportedFilter instead of being applied — protocol misbehavior that is not a compile error.'

MailboxFilterCondition is #[non_exhaustive] so the rustc exhaustiveness check cannot enforce this. A well-intentioned contributor adds a 5th field (e.g. 'sortOrder' filter) to MailboxFilterCondition, the list here doesn't get updated, and clients sending the new filter receive unsupportedFilter responses for what is now a legitimate filter. The bug is silent — tests for the new field would catch it only if they invoke the full /query path, not unit tests on the type.

Two options:

1. Use a compile-time const computed from MailboxFilterCondition by exporting an array of known wire-key names from jmap-mail-types. Single source of truth; rustc enforces.

2. Drop the pre-validation entirely and let serde return an 'unknown field' error during from_value (with #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on MailboxFilterCondition). Pre-1.0 the wire-format check is well-defined, but RFC 8620 §5.5 unsupportedFilter is more specific than serde's generic error, so converting the serde error type to unsupportedFilter is the right boundary anyway.

Option 1 keeps the current wire-error shape; option 2 trades a generic 'unknown field' message for the eliminated drift risk. Either fixes the latent maintainer-burden cost.
title: KNOWN_FILTER_KEYS list drifts silently from MailboxFilterCondition
